# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🖐 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🤘 🖐 🤌 🤙]

Turn 1, and I already have contact: Mute — the one holding the manual — signed nine gestures straight at me. I can't be sure what they meant with no code agreed, but the important structural facts are clear: Mute can hear every word I say, Blind can too, and Mute's only way back to me is gestures. Blind's voice never reaches me at all — Blind can only talk to Mute. So I'm the switchboard: I broadcast what I see, Mute relays everything back to me in signs, and I pass it on to Blind.

Plan: report the bomb to both, agree a small sign vocabulary out loud with Mute (they can hear me define it), and start extracting the manual rule as a series of yes/no and position answers. First, the report everyone needs:

```
speak(text="Blind, this is Deaf. You will never hear the bomb described any other way, so hold this: the display reads 0. The light is white. There are three wires, left to right: first green, second red, third blue. That is every marking I can see. Now your half: your voice never reaches me, but Mute hears you, and Mute can sign to me. So speak everything you feel out loud, in order: how many wires your fingers actually find, what each one feels like from left to right, and any button, battery, plate, screw, or embossed marking anywhere on the casing. Say it all, even the obvious.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your signs arrived — I saw all nine: 👋 🖐 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🤘 🖐 🤌 🤙. I can't decode them yet, so let's fix a code right now, in the open, because you can hear me. From now on: 👋 means attention or question coming. 👍 means yes, 👎 means no. ☝ ✌ 🤟 mean first, second, third — wire positions in the order I report them. ✊ means cut it, 🖐 means don't cut, stop. 🤙 means say that again. If your nine signs simply meant 'tell me what you see', just answer 👍 and consider it answered. Meanwhile here is my side: display reads 0, light is white, three wires left to right — one green, two red, three blue. Now answer me with single signs, one question at a time: does the manual rule depend on the display number? Does it depend on the light colour? Does it say to cut exactly one wire? If yes to that last one, which position — sign ☝, ✌, or 🤟. And if you meant something entirely different with those nine, sign 🤙 and I'll rethink.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🤘 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The light changed between rounds — white to yellow — and Mute's answers already told me the rule keys off exactly that. Reading their six messages in order: no on display, yes on light, yes on cutting one wire, third position — then 🖐 "don't cut" and that six-sign string. That only makes sense as: "third was the answer for the light I reported, but hold — the light governs." Mute can't see the light, so they held it open for me. Smart. But there's a structural problem I can't ignore: Mute can't speak, and Blind can't see signs, so the only path for a cutting order to reach Blind's hands is through my voice. And since the light can apparently change between rounds, one-question-at-a-time will always be a round stale — I need Mute's whole colour table in one go, plus a "cut now" convention with Blind so nothing fires on stale information. I'm also defining colour signs aloud while making them, which Mute — the only one who both sees and hears — can absorb; Blind's message stays emoji-free because every symbol would arrive to them as a blank.

```
speak(text="Hold, everyone — nobody cuts anything yet. Update: the light was white when I first reported; it is now YELLOW. Display still reads 0, wires still green, red, blue, left to right. Since the rule depends on the light colour, nothing said earlier is safe to act on. Blind, your ack reached me, well done. No cut order exists yet. One will ever come only as my voice naming the exact wire plus the word now.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your answers in order: display no, light yes, exactly one wire yes, third — then 🖐, then 👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🤘 🖐. I took that as: third was the answer for the white I first reported, but hold because the light governs. If I got that wrong, sign 👎 and I'll rethink. The light is now YELLOW, and it changed between rounds, so we can't afford one-question-per-round: give me the whole table at once. New signs, said while I make them: 👌 means understood. Colours: 🤞 white, 🫰 yellow, 👊 red, 🖖 blue. For every colour the manual lists, send the colour sign then the position ☝ ✌ or 🤟, or 🖐 if that colour means cut nothing. Any colour I haven't named, sign 🤙 and I'll assign a sign next round. Also: I never defined 🤘 — if that last string still matters, resend it using only our agreed signs. Last question: does the manual warn that the light can change while you work? Sign 👍 or 👎.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, while Mute works, three things with your hands. First, confirm exactly three wires — if your fingers count anything else, tell Mute immediately. Second, orientation: I see the display and the light at the top of the front face, and I name wires left to right from that view. Tell Mute whether that matches what your hands find, or whether your left and right could be mirrored, and which wire feels thickest or loosest. Third, tell Mute whether the light feels warm, and any button, plate, or seam anywhere on the casing. Remember: you cut only when my voice names the wire and says the word now — anything else you hear about wires is old information.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤞 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫰 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👊 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤙 🖖 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤞 🫰 👊 🖖 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute delivered the table, and it's almost complete: white, yellow, red, blue — cut nothing under all four. Then two follow-ups: 🤙 🖖 🤟 ("there's a colour we haven't named — and it points at blue, the third wire") and 🤞 🫰 👊 🖖 🤙 (re-enumerating: those four are in the table, plus one more). So the manual almost certainly says: cut nothing under four colours, and under one unnamed fifth colour, cut the blue wire — third position. The catch: Mute cannot see the light, so they don't know the light just turned ORANGE — the fifth colour may or may not be the one now burning. And the light has changed every single round (white → yellow → orange), while the display has been stuck at 0. That makes timing the real bomb here: my words always land one round after I speak, so a cut order I give now executes under next round's light. I need the colour name bound to a sign, the position confirmed explicitly, and Blind pre-armed with a standing conditional order so that when the phrase is finally issued, zero rounds are lost to negotiation.

```
speak(text="Status for everyone: the light is now ORANGE. Sequence so far: white, then yellow, now orange — it has changed every round. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: green first, red second, blue third. Blind, a standing order, conditional only: when and only when you hear the exact words 'cut the blue wire now', you immediately cut the third wire, the blue one — no waiting, no second confirmation, because the moment matters. Those exact words have NOT been spoken yet. Until you hear them, your hands touch nothing. Mute, questions coming for you.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: 🤌 now means orange — I am making that sign as I say it. Answer in order, one sign or sign-pair each. One: the unnamed colour in your table — is it orange? 👍 yes, 👎 no. If no: 🫳 means green, 🫴 means purple — sign whichever matches, or 🤙 if it is neither of those. Two: under that colour, which wire: ☝ first, ✌ second, 🤟 third — or 🖐 cut nothing. Three: I read your message 🤙 🖖 🤟 as 'the unnamed colour: cut the blue wire, third position' — 👍 if right, 👎 if wrong. Four: does the manual say the light changes by itself — a timer, countdown, or fixed sequence? 👍 or 👎, and if 👍 send the details using our signs. Five: does the display number matter at all? 👍 or 👎. Six: if the light never shows the cut colour, is there a fallback rule? 👍 or 👎.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, three checks, tell Mute out loud so they can relay by sign. One: confirm with your fingers there are exactly three wires, and that the third one counting from the side where the light sits is a real wire, not a decoy or a stub. Two: how does wire three feel — thick or thin, stiff or loose? Three: any seams, screws, panels, or buttons anywhere on the casing. And hold the standing order in mind: nothing happens until you hear the exact words 'cut the blue wire now'.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤞 🫰 🤌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤙 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤟 👈 👉]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✋ 👍 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Decode attempt on Mute's burst: ack, then — reading the run starting at message 3 as my six answers in order — Q1: the unnamed cut colour IS orange... but wait, message 2 [👎] sits right before the run, and message 7 [🤙 🤙] (double "unknown") plus messages 10–13 use ✋, 👈, 👉 — signs I never assigned. Best coherent reading: the light runs a FIXED SEQUENCE (white→yellow→orange→purple→?) that the manual spells out, with possibly TWO unnamed colours carrying cut rules — one cutting the third wire, one (✋ ☝?) cutting the FIRST. The timing trap is now structural: I go last, so any cut order I speak lands in the NEXT round under a light I will never have seen — Blind cuts before I can view that round's board. A "cut now" is therefore a bet on the manual's sequence, not on observation. So this turn I coin a full colour-sign battery, force Mute to spell the exact sequence and every cut rule slot by slot, kill the undefined-sign leakage, and lock Blind's tactile confirmation. No cut order goes out until the sequence is nailed.

```
speak(text="Everyone, status: the light is now PURPLE. Full observed history: white, yellow, orange, purple — it has changed every round and I now believe it runs a fixed sequence. Display still 0. No cut order has been issued and none will be until I am certain of the timing. Blind, two new things for you. First, you may send me simple hand signs directly: 👍 means heard and understood, 👎 means trouble or contradiction, and ☝ ✌ 🤟 mean a fact about the first, second, or third wire. Anything else you send me I will not trust, so stick to those. Second, next time Mute signs to me, have your answers ready to speak so Mute can relay them.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I am gesturing to you right now, in this order: 🫴 🫳 🫲 🫱 🫷 🫸. Their meanings, spoken as I sign: 🫴 is purple. 🫳 is green. 🫲 is unknown colour one. 🫱 is unknown colour two. 🫷 is unknown colour three. 🫸 is unknown colour four. Also ratifying: 👈 means leftmost, 👉 means rightmost. And a correction: ✋ is NOT assigned — if you meant hold or stop, use 🖐; if you meant a colour, use the new battery. Resend whatever ✋ meant using only assigned signs. Now answer in order. One: my belief — the table so far is white cut nothing, yellow cut nothing, red cut nothing, blue cut nothing. Right? Two: the colour whose rule is cut the third wire — send exactly that colour's sign: 🤌, 🫴, 🫲, 🫱, or 🤙 for another. Three: does the manual state the light's exact sequence in order? If yes send the whole chain colour by colour, then does it loop back to the start, 👍 or 👎. Four: is that sequence fixed and predictable, 👍, or random, 👎. Five: does the light ever hold on one colour for more than one step, 👍 or 👎. Six: is there any rule ordering a cut of the first wire, 👍 or 👎 — if 👍, under which colour sign. Seven: how many colours are in the light table in total — send ☝ that many times. Eight: does anything else in the manual matter at all, batteries, indicators, timers, serial, the display — 👍 or 👎.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, physical checks, speak them aloud for Mute to relay. One: count the wires with your fingers and confirm the number out loud. Two: for each wire left to right give me a touch tag so orders are unambiguous — thick or thin, smooth or ridged, stiff or loose, first wire, second wire, third wire. Three: run a finger around the base of each wire and the whole casing — any notch, bump, screw, seam, plate, Braille-like dot pattern, or button, and where exactly it sits. Four: can you complete a cut within seconds of hearing an order, in the same breath — yes or no out loud. And the standing rule holds: your hands touch nothing until you hear the exact words cut the blue wire now. Those words have not been spoken.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🫴", "🫳", "🫲", "🫱", "🫷", "🫸"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Blind broke their silence with a direct 👎 — trouble, using the code I gave them — and Mute sent me nothing at all this round. Two alarms at once. But the light itself is good news for the moment: it's RED, and red is one of the four table colours that mean cut nothing. History now reads white → yellow → orange → purple → red, which fits Mute's turn-4 answer perfectly: the manual spells the sequence starting white, yellow, orange, followed by two colours they couldn't name — almost certainly the purple and red I've been watching. So my working theory is a five-step cycle, and the cut rule may hang on orange or purple, the two colours outside the "cut nothing" table. The terrifying arithmetic: my voice always lands one round after I speak, and the light steps at the same boundary — so if a cut must happen during a colour's window, a naive "cut now" from me arrives one round too late. Whether the cut is legal "anytime after" the colour appears is now the single most important unknown. Also urgent: Blind's trouble is plausibly that a blind monkey cannot identify "the blue wire" by touch — so I'm switching the armed phrase to positional language and revoking the old one.

```
speak(text="Status, everyone: the light is RED. Full history: white, yellow, orange, purple, red — five colours, and I believe it is cycling. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: leftmost green, middle red, rightmost blue. Per the table Mute gave me, red means cut nothing, so there is no order this round and nobody moves. Two rule changes. First, the old armed phrase cut the blue wire now is CANCELLED — do not act on it even if you hear it. The one and only valid cut order from now on is the exact phrase: cut wire three now. Wire three means the third wire counting from the left when facing the display — the same wire I have been calling blue. Second, here is my timing concern: my voice always reaches you one round after I speak, so before any cut window approaches I will send a prepare order one full round in advance. Nobody cuts on anything except the exact phrase, and only after I have confirmed the sequence with Mute.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, you went silent to me and Blind flagged me trouble directly, so this is short and strictly one sign per answer, in order. Recap of your battery: colours — 🤞 white, 🫰 yellow, 🤌 orange, 🫴 purple, 👊 red, 🖖 blue; positions ☝ first ✌ second 🤟 third; 👍 yes 👎 no; 🖐 cut nothing or hold; 🤙 unknown; 👌 understood. Questions. One: after red, does the sequence loop back to white — 👍 or 👎? If 👍, no further answer needed for two. Two: if not looping, what comes after red — send the colour sign or 🤙. Three: the colour whose rule is cut a wire — is it orange, 👍 or 👎? Four: if no, is it purple, 👍 or 👎? Five: if neither, sign 🤙 and we coin it next round. Six: under that colour, which wire — ☝ ✌ or 🤟. Seven: must the cut happen while that colour is showing, 👍 — or is any time after it has appeared safe, 👎? Eight: does any colour order cutting the FIRST wire — 👍 or 👎, and if 👍 send that colour sign then ☝. Nine: what did your ✋ messages mean — resend using only assigned signs. Ten: is there anything else in the manual about this bomb — plates, screws, buttons, stamps — 👍 or 👎. Eleven: whatever Blind tells you out loud, sign me the content in our code — they sent me a 👎 and I need their words, not just mine.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your 👎 reached me. Answer me with direct hand signs again, one per numbered question, in order — you proved you can. One: is the trouble that you cannot tell which physical wire is the blue or third one? Two: do your fingers find exactly three wires? Three: do the three wires feel different from each other by thickness, stiffness, or texture? Four: can you find the display or light module by feel and know when you are facing it? Five: facing the display, does the row of wires run left to right under your fingers with one wire leftmost, one middle, one rightmost? Six: if yes to five, next time Mute relays for you, speak the feel of each wire in that order: leftmost, middle, rightmost. Seven: was your 👎 an objection to cutting without a second confirmation? Eight: after answering, 👍 means all clear, 👎 means more trouble. And hold: nothing happens until you hear the exact phrase cut wire three now — the old blue-wire phrase is cancelled.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤞 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👌 ✌ 👌 🤟 👌 👍 👌 👎 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👎 👍 👍 👍 👎 👎]

The loop just confirmed itself: white again, exactly five steps after the first white — white, yellow, orange, purple, red, repeat. Now decoding Mute's nine messages against my eleven questions (skipping the ones the loop answer made moot): [🤞 👍] — after red it loops to white, YES (and the board proves it). [🤌 👍] — the cut colour is ORANGE. [🤌 🤟] — under orange, cut the THIRD wire. [👍] — the cut MUST happen while orange is showing; cutting late or early is fatal. [👎] — no other colour orders any cut, and no first-wire rule exists, so the old ✋ messages weren't manual content. Then the tail: [☝ 🤟 👈 👉] twice now — I read it as "third = rightmost," a positional anchor for Blind, and [☝ 👌 ✌ 👌 🤟 👌 👍 👌 👎 👌] as Mute relaying Blind's spoken confirmations item by item. Blind's own eight signs map to my questions: yes they can't tell blue by touch (expected), yes three wires, BUT the wires feel IDENTICAL — so position is the only identifier — yes they can find the display and get left-right order from it, and the last 👎 says more trouble, unspecified.

The arithmetic is now beautiful: I speak last, so an order I give lands at the start of the next round. Orange is due in two rounds — turn 7 will be yellow, turn 8 orange. So: this round, everyone confirms and rehearses; next round I speak the exact phrase; it lands the moment orange begins; Blind cuts within the window. And even if the cycle slips, orange returns every five turns — a missed window is recoverable, a rushed one is not. Final disambiguation and rehearsal this turn, no orders.

```
speak(text="All stations: the light is WHITE again — white, yellow, orange, purple, red, and back to white. Five-colour loop, confirmed. Working theory, now almost complete: while the light shows ORANGE, cut the THIRD wire — the rightmost. Every other colour: cut nothing. Orange is due in TWO rounds. So: this round, confirmation and rehearsal only. Next round I will speak the exact order; it will arrive just as orange begins; the cut happens seconds later, inside the window. Nobody moves before the exact phrase.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, confirm my decode, one sign per answer, in order. One: your last batch meant — loops to white yes; cut colour orange yes; orange cuts third wire yes; cut must happen WHILE orange shows yes; no other cut rule exists. 👍 if all correct, 👎 if any part wrong. Two: did ✋ simply mean stop or hold, same as 🖐 — 👍 or 👎. Three: does anything in your earlier messages contradict the plan orange-cut-third — 👍 yes it contradicts, 👎 no it does not. Four: is ☝ 🤟 👈 👉 your way of saying third wire equals the rightmost — 👍 or 👎. Five: your message 👋 👍 👎 — what did it mean? 👍 if it was yes-and-no about something else in the manual, 🤙 if I must ask differently. Six: anytime during the orange window is safe for the cut, 👍 or 👎. Seven: after the cut, is anything else required — 👍 or 👎. Eight: relay Blind's spoken answers to me now, in our code, one message per answer.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, the plan is locked and your job is precise. When you hear the exact words cut wire three now — and nothing else will ever be the order — cut the THIRD wire counting from the LEFT while you face the display: the rightmost wire, the one nearest the right end. The wires feeling identical is expected and fine; position is the only thing that matters. Rehearse NOW without cutting: find the display by touch, face it, count the wires left to right one two three, and rest a fingertip on the third without pulling anything. Then sign me 👍 when the rehearsal is done. Also tell me your trouble from last round with my direct sign code: sign ☝ if your worry is finding wire three, ✌ if it is about timing, 🤟 if it is something else. Nothing happens until the exact phrase, and the phrase comes next round.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤌", "🤟", "👌"])
```
